data.name: Masla
data.gender_notes: Masla is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'asalaha', meaning 'to be in good health'. The name Masla evokes images of grace, slenderness, and elegance. In Islamic tradition, it is said to symbolize the delicate balance between physical and spiritual well-being. The name Masla carries the meaning “Slender, Delicate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Masla usually hope their child will grow to embody slender, delicate and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Masla belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Slender, Delicate.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Masla total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

In many Islamic cultures, the name is given to babies as a wish for their good health and well-being. Masla is also a popular name among Arabic-speaking communities around the world, reflecting the importance of health and wellness in their traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: Beyond its literal meaning, Masla carries deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture. It represents the idea that true health and wellness come from within, through a balanced and compassionate lifestyle. Masla encourages us to prioritize our spiritual growth alongside our physical health, and to strive for harmony between the two. Additionally, the name is a reminder that every individual has the power to improve their own well-being and that of their community, making Masla an inspiring and meaningful name for those seeking personal growth and spiritual enlightenment.
